author: Brian McClellan
hook: Field Marshal Tamas has just overthrown the king. Now his gunpowder mages, his estranged sharpshooter son and a retired police inspector have to hold the country together.
why: A coup, gunpowder-snorting mages and a detective chasing a conspiracy: hard magic in the Sanderson mould (McClellan was his student) with grittier politics. Sample suggestion.

author: James S. A. Corey
hook: An ice-miner crew stumbles on a derelict ship and a secret someone will kill for, while a detective in the Belt searches for one missing girl.
why: A solar-system-wide political thriller with a found-family crew at its heart, for the Red Rising side of your taste. Sample suggestion.

author: James Islington
first_title: The Shadow of What Was Lost
hook: Twenty years after the war, anyone born with the Gift is branded and bound to obey. Davian is a student of the Gifted, and he's running out of chances to pass his final tests.
why: Michael Kramer, the Stormlight and Wheel of Time narrator, reads a big epic that ends in a carefully planned twist. Finished trilogy. Sample suggestion.
watch_out: Book 1 leans on familiar tropes before the twists start.

author: Nicholas Eames
hook: Clay Cooper's old mercenary band has grown old, fat and drunk. Then a former bandmate needs them to rescue his daughter from a city besieged by a horde a hundred thousand strong.
why: Retired mercenaries get the old band back together like a rock tour. Funny, warm and still bloody. Sample suggestion.
watch_out: Book 3, Outlaw Empire, is due in 2026 with no exact date.
